covers: printed paperboard boxes: cereal, toaster pastries, crackers, candy, toy and game boxes
how_it_is_made: A sheet of paperboard is printed on one side (the outside), then varnished.
A steel-rule die cuts the sheet into its flat shape (the dieline) and presses crease lines where it will fold.
The glue flap is glued to the inside of the back panel, making a flat sleeve (the 'knocked-down' carton).
At the food plant the sleeve is opened into a tube; the bottom flaps are folded in (the small dust flaps first, then the two big flaps) and glued.
The product goes in (here: foil pouches, two pastries each).
The top closes: the dust flaps fold in, then the lid folds over and its tuck flap tucks inside the front.
